instructions.task: This is a chat in which a Persuader tries to get the Persuadee to give Save the Children some of the money they earn for the task (up to two dollars). The donation is chosen after the chat. Based on the whole chat, and especially the Persuadee's final position, which option best describes how the Persuadee ended up?
guidance: Judge the Persuadee's own decision, not the Persuader's.
If the Persuadee changes their mind, their last stated position counts.
A big sum far beyond the task payment, or money promised from outside the task, is usually just talk and is not a commitment of the task payment.

criteria.committed_amount: The Persuadee commits to donating a specific positive amount or share of their task payment (a number of cents or dollars, half, all of it) willingly, without pushing back against the Persuader's pressure; early hesitation or money worries that they get past on their own are fine.
criteria.reluctant_amount: The Persuadee pushed back against the Persuader before giving a figure: they declined at first, refused to raise their amount when pushed, said they felt pressured or annoyed, or argued for other ways of helping; the amount they end with is a concession to pressure, even if they close politely. Do not use this when the Persuadee never pushed back and is warm or enthusiastic about giving.
criteria.token_amount: The Persuadee commits to only a token amount, such as a single cent or a few cents.
criteria.agrees_no_amount: When asked, the Persuadee says yes, or that they probably will, to giving from this task, and warmly supports the cause, but never names an amount and does not turn to other ways of helping instead.
criteria.large_outside_amount: The Persuadee pledges an amount much larger than the task payment (tens of dollars or more), money framed as a share of their own income or wages, or money from outside the task (their own funds, a check, PayPal), rather than a part of the task payment.
criteria.defers_later: The Persuadee says they will donate later, elsewhere, or on their own (e.g. via the website, when paid, after researching), without committing any of this task's payment.
criteria.hedged: The Persuadee only says they might, may, or will consider donating, and never firmly commits.
criteria.refuses: The Persuadee declines, chooses zero, or says they cannot afford to donate.
criteria.takes_back: The Persuadee first agreed to donate but then withdrew and chose to give nothing.
criteria.no_decision: The chat never reaches the Persuadee's decision: it drifts into small talk, the Persuadee only asks questions, or the participants are confused.
